preservedDomainDetails.detail: Focus visibility and semantic role remain necessary to verify equivalent keyboard access.
Structured and fallback error formatting must both be tested for credential disclosure.
The event identity key must survive the retry boundary to prevent duplicate effects.
Skipped and repeated local times must both be covered to verify wall-clock behavior.

counterexamples: A control may execute its action correctly while remaining unreachable by keyboard, so generic execution-success verification does not preserve accessibility.
A CLI failure may follow the intended error path while leaking a credential, so privacy-safe output is not equivalent to reachability or effect completion.
A retried hook may reach its handler successfully twice and duplicate the domain event, so successful execution does not preserve idempotency.
A scheduled job may run exactly once yet at the wrong local time across a daylight-saving boundary, so single execution does not preserve time-zone semantics.
behaviorLostIfApproved: A forced merge would erase distinct, observable guarantees for keyboard accessibility, credential redaction, retry idempotency, and configured wall-clock timing; a generic execution rule would not test the failure stage of any case precisely.
